status.main_product: Digital network and SaaS solutions for trade finance operations
status.scope_reason: The company builds and operates Global Trade Konnect (GTK) and Konsole, which are multi-bank platforms and digital networks designed for managing and automating trade finance instruments like letters of credit and guarantees.
status.evidence: According to Komgo's official product updates and profiles, the company provides multi-bank SaaS applications and a secure digital network explicitly built for managing trade finance workflows and connecting corporates with financial institutions.

claims.claim: Independent verification shows that Crédit Agricole CIB utilizes Komgo's multibank integration layer to route and execute structured digital workflows for documentary credits, standby letters of credit, bank guarantees, and collections.
claims.source: https://ca-cib.en

claims.claim: The company reports that its Global Trade Konnect application, launched in April 2025, utilizes integrated artificial intelligence to compare transaction data, extract info from draft invoices, and automate document checking.
claims.source: https://www.gtreview.com/news/digital-trade/komgo-launches-global-trade-konnect-in-major-system-upgrade/

claims.claim: A partnership established by the company with Complidata in 2025 adds AI-assisted document checking capabilities focused directly on trade document accuracy.
claims.source: https://www.komgo.io/

claims.claim: The company reports that its platform integrates directly with the SWIFT network using its proprietary Swift key via Swift's NOSU solution, and it supports the commercialized ICC-Swift API standards for bank guarantees.
claims.source: https://www.komgo.io/newsroom/komgo-and-swift-strengthen-collaboration-to-elevate-trade-finance-connectivity

claims.claim: Komgo collaborated with FIATA to implement the electronic forwarder's bill of lading (eFBL) data standard using its blockchain-based Trakk solution to allow the secure tracking and authentication of digital shipping documents.
claims.source: https://www.gtreview.com/news/digital-trade/fiata-partners-with-komgo-on-electronic-forwarders-bill-of-lading/

claims.claim: Komgo reports that its infrastructure utilizes a secure cloud-native SaaS deployment model delivering decentralized digital connectivity via the Konsole multi-bank network. The architecture is underpinned by an enterprise Ethereum distributed ledger technology framework (built on Quorum) featuring a proprietary document transfer mechanism called Kite that supports secure peer-to-peer data validation and privacy by design.
claims.source: Consensys case study (https://consensys.io/blockchain-use-cases/finance/komgo) and Komgo documentation outlining Quorum and Kite framework.

claims.claim: The company reports offering extensive open API integration capability (including compliance with ICC-SWIFT API standards) to connect seamlessly with banks' back-office core systems, corporate ERP, and TMS solutions, processing nearly one billion dollars in financial transactions across its network daily.
claims.source: Komgo FAQ (https://www.komgo.io/faq) confirming $1 billion in daily transaction value and industry standard alignment with ICC-Swift API specifications.

claims.claim: The company reports the rollout of Global Trade Konnect (GTK) in April 2025, which serves as its consolidated SaaS application merging multi-bank trade finance workflows with embedded artificial intelligence tools including an LC Creation Agent, Digital Reporting Assistant, and Smart Clause Checker.
claims.source: Komgo Newsroom announcements from April 2025 regarding the flagship launch of Global Trade Konnect (GTK) along with its feature documentation outlining embedded generative AI assistants (https://www.komgo.io/newsroom/introducing-gtk-future-of-digital-guarantee-and-trade-finance-management).

claims.claim: In September 2026, the company announced a collaboration with Crédit Agricole CIB to integrate AI-powered capabilities into the bank's Optimtrade digital trade finance portal.
claims.source: Official press release published on Komgo Newsroom on September 24, 2026, titled 'Crédit Agricole CIB and Komgo collaborate to bring AI-powered capabilities to Optimtrade' (https://komgo.io).

claims.claim: Komgo reports that its multibank trade finance platform connects more than 300 corporates and financial institutions across 50 countries, with specific shareholders and users including global entities such as BNP Paribas, Citibank, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), Crédit Agricole CIB, TotalEnergies, Shell, Gunvor, and Koch Supply & Trading.
claims.source: Komgo corporate info page and ecosystem updates detailing network size of over 300 corporates and financial institutions across 50 countries, as well as founding shareholder records (https://www.komgo.io/about).

claims.claim: Publicly announced customer deployments include ANDRITZ deploying Komgo's Global Trade Konnect (GTK) solution across 40 countries to digitalize communications with 30+ financing partners, Standard Chartered executing its first ICC-SWIFT API standards bank guarantee transaction via Komgo, and case studies highlighting active utilization by Siemens Healthineers, Baker Hughes, Société Générale, and DBS Bank.
claims.source: Komgo Newsroom (ANDRITZ press release, Nov 2025); Standard Chartered Press Release (Jan 2026); Komgo GTK Solutions page (Siemens Healthineers, Baker Hughes cases)

claims.claim: The company reported a 50 percent increase in trade finance transactions flowing through its platform alongside a 65 percent year-over-year increase in clients operating in production.
claims.corrected: The company reported a 50 percent increase in trade finance transactions flowing through its platform alongside a 65 percent increase in clients in the past year.
claims.source: ING Ventures / Komgo Funding Announcement (June 2021); PYMNTS

claims.claim: Komgo SA expanded its corporate reach and operational volumes by acquiring GlobalTrade Corporation (GTC), which allowed the combined entity to service over 120 multinational clients and 11,000 subsidiaries.
claims.source: Komgo Newsroom / Business Wire (Dec 2022 Acquisition Press Release)

claims.claim: The company reports strengthening its physical footprint in the Americas by opening a hub office in Miami in April 2024, staffed with a regional Managing Director, sales executives, and account executives.
claims.corrected: The company reports strengthening its physical footprint in the Americas by opening a hub office in Miami in June 2024, staffed with a regional Managing Director, sales executives, and account executives.
claims.source: Komgo Newsroom (June 2024 Press Release: 'Komgo Strengthens Americas Presence with New Miami Office')

claims.claim: Komgo SA was launched in 2018 as an independent venture backed by a consortium of 15 founding corporate and banking shareholders, including ABN Amro, BNP Paribas, Citi, Crédit Agricole, Gunvor, ING, Koch Supply & Trading, Macquarie, Mercuria, MUFG Bank, Natixis, Rabobank, Shell, SGS, and Société Générale.
claims.source: SGS Co-launches komgo Press Release (Sept 2018); Global Trade Review (GTR)

claims.claim: The company successfully closed a third equity funding round in May 2021, raising CHF 26 million (approximately $28.9 million) from returning shareholders alongside new investor Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC) and an additional unnamed financial institution. Subsequent strategic equity investments were executed by Santander Corporate & Investment Banking and Emirates NBD's Innovation Fund in June 2023 and September 2023 respectively, expanding the ownership base to 24 institutional backers.
claims.note: The exact total count of institutional backers following the 2023 investments is unconfirmed (sources show Komgo already had 24 investors by July 2022).
claims.source: Komgo Press Releases & Webflow Funding Announcement (May 2021), Finextra (September 2023), Santander Press Release (June 2023), Komgo Newsroom (July 2022)

claims.claim: The company reports connecting more than 60 banks and over 10,000 corporate users across 50 countries on its multi-bank trade finance digital network.
claims.source: Komgo Newsroom (July 2025, December 2025)

status.event: Renamed to TKDIGITAL HOLDINGS PTE. LTD. (previously RABC HOLDINGS PTE. LTD.)
status.main_product: BANCO transaction banking and supply-chain finance platform
status.scope_reason: The company provides the BANCO supply-chain finance platform which connects enterprises and financial institutions for digital trade and supply chain financing.
status.evidence: According to Singapore ACRA registry records via Scam.sg, the company with UEN 201919616G changed its name from RootAnt to RABC Holdings and subsequently to TKDIGITAL HOLDINGS PTE. LTD.

claims.claim: The company reports that its BANCO platform utilizes R3's Corda enterprise blockchain network to manage data exchange, privacy, and transaction validation for multi-tier supply chain financing.
claims.source: Ledger Insights; SBI Holdings Presentation (July 2021)

claims.claim: In September 2021, the company partnered with Marketnode and SETL to develop end-to-end infrastructure for fixed-income and multi-asset documentation and data processing.
claims.source: The Business Times; Yahoo Finance

claims.claim: The company reports its Digital Banking-as-a-Service software model is built on a modular and microservices architecture with Open APIs available for ecosystem partner integration.
claims.source: RABC Group Official Site (RootAnt Digital About Page); e27 Startup Profile

claims.claim: The company reports that its deep-tier supply chain finance platform, BANCO, connects buyers and sellers with financing providers on the R3 Corda and Hyperledger Fabric blockchain protocols.
claims.source: Fintech Futures Press Release; Hunter Technology Corporate Updates

claims.claim: The company expanded its capabilities on September 29, 2021, by launching a central lending platform called BANCR to integrate multi-funder digital lending directly into its BANCO transaction banking platform.
claims.source: IBS Intelligence; Retail Banker International; Finextra

claims.claim: RootAnt signed an agreement in 2021 with Bank of China to deploy a digital trade financing platform enabling branches in Singapore and Chongqing, alongside traders and logistics companies, to exchange electronic trade documents.
claims.source: Monetary Authority of Singapore Official Speech (7 December 2021)

claims.claim: RootAnt (rebranded as banco) established a strategic corporate partnership with real estate services firm Savills to deploy its finance platform.
claims.source: Savills Singapore Press Release (29 March 2022) / PR Newswire

claims.claim: The company signed an agreement with the Bank of China to serve as a trade financing platform on the Singapore side under the CCI-ILSTC framework, verified by the Monetary Authority of Singapore.
claims.source: RootAnt / RABC Group Official Website / Monetary Authority of Singapore Official Speech

claims.claim: The Business Times verified that the company secured nearly US$1.5 million in a seed funding round in October 2020, led by Linear Capital alongside co-investor KZM & Company Group.
claims.source: The Business Times (2 October 2020)

claims.claim: In March 2021, SBI Group's local subsidiary BYFIN partnered with RootAnt Global to launch the blockchain-oriented "SBI-BANCO" Deep-Tier Supply Chain Finance Platform in the APAC region.
claims.source: SBI Holdings Press Release (16 March 2021) / IBS Intelligence (25 March 2021)

claims.claim: Marketnode partnered with RootAnt Global and SETL to focus on fixed income and multi-asset end-to-end digital infrastructure development.
claims.source: https://www.thetradenews.com/marketnode-announces-partners-ahead-of-upcoming-product-launches/
